label: Input digit "2" during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Fires on every step where the input token is the digit 2 during the original-sequence phase (precision 1.0, recall ~0.997 on dev). Magnitude is highest (~max) when 2 is the first token of the sequence and when it is the first occurrence of 2; repeat occurrences of 2 and 2s later in the original sequence get weaker activations (e.g. 0.8-0.9 mid-sequence, as low as 0.1-0.5 near the end of long sequences, from examples). It does not fire on any other token, on <DEL>, or on 2s fed back during the copy phase, except for tiny (~0.0-0.1) residual activations when 2 is echoed back at recall_idx 1 in sequences that started with 2 (0% of mass).

issues: Checked on test: P 1.000, R 0.997, F1 0.999, mass recall 0.9998. There are 0 false positives. All 286 missed steps (0.0% of activation mass) match (phase==2)&(in_tok==2)&(recall_idx==1)&(orig(0)==2). Scoring that predicate alone gives recall 0.00265, which accounts for every miss. Its precision is only 1.7%, so these are scattered leftover activations (relative activation about 0.02-0.08), not a firing class worth adding.

The magnitude claims hold up. Activation-mass share falls steadily with t: 0.21 at t=0 down to 0.006 at t=8. The firing rate is flat across orig_idx (about 0.034). Top examples are all 2 as the first token at 1.00. A repeated 2 reaches about 0.8-0.88, and late 2s in the lowest quartile are about 0.14-0.49. in_first=1 carries 93% of the mass.
Zero activation on <DEL> and on every non-2 token is confirmed. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
Minor imprecision: the copy-phase leftovers appear when 2 is fed back as the input at recall_idx 1, meaning the echo of orig(0)=2. Calling it 'the second copied output' is close enough.
